chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the elderly man and the elderly woman who are too weak to fast in the month of Ramadan. He said: They give charity for each day with a mud of wheat.

key_terms.تَضْعُفُ عَنِ الصَّوْمِ: Weak in fasting / too weak to fast
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A specific volume measure used in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for an elderly person who cannot fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the specific mechanism of fidyah for the elderly who cannot fast due to permanent weakness, distinguishing it from temporary illness. It specifies the exact measure of one mud of wheat per day, reflecting the prophetic tradition's emphasis on tangible sustenance for the poor. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that fidyah is a compensatory charity rather than a penalty, ensuring the elderly remain spiritually connected to Ramadan through consistent giving.
